fix: Add to the builder AND tdd-engineer personas a hard deliverable requirement: for every new exported symbol, option, field, gate, or CLI flag, the report must NAME its production caller and cite the test that proves the seam is REACHED from that caller (not merely that the seam works when called directly). A seam whose only caller is a test is dead code and must be declared as such or deleted. Then make it checkable: extend the build-handoff floor with a cheap heuristic — new exported symbol or new flag with zero non-test references in the diff's package set → WARN with the exact prescription. Predicate authoring guidance follows: a wiring proof is a reachability test, not a unit test.
notes: From the 2026-07-30 LLM-stability review §6. This is the highest-confidence item in that review because the evidence is first-hand and it recurred three times in different forms.
summary: First-hand evidence 2026-07-30: two console implementer agents produced high-quality tested work from precise prompts, and BOTH under-optimized integration — one added a struct field with no consumer (dead plumbing, caught in review), the other built a lint with NO CALLER at all (the natural call site runs before its inputs exist). They satisfied the stated contract exactly and did not infer the unstated one. The same class recurs in loop cycles: the P2 accounting seam wired only into the sequential loop body was unreachable in fleet mode (#373), and ADR-0074's typed routing shipped inert once before. This repo HAS a 'wiring proof mandatory' policy — but it lives in operator lore, so agents never inherit it.
title: Builder/TDD personas must require CALLER PROOF for every new seam — integration is an acceptance criterion, not an assumption
